name: Bachelor of Business
description:
Holmes's Bachelor of Business is a 24-unit, three-year degree with four specialisation options (Management, Marketing, International Business and Hospitality Management), the last of which is a slightly unusual inclusion for a business-only private provider and reflects Holmes's history of teaching hospitality alongside its commerce offerings. Students complete a shared core of accounting, economics, law and management units in years one and two before specialising in year three.

As with most of Holmes's degrees, the cohort is heavily international, and the degree functions for a lot of students as the standard three-year pathway toward permanent residency via the skilled migration points test, rather than purely as an academic credential chosen on its own merits. That's not a criticism of the teaching: the core units are solid and cover the same ground as equivalent degrees at larger universities. But it's worth naming plainly rather than pretending every enrolment is driven by intellectual interest in business theory.
curriculum:
Year 1: Accounting for Business Decisions; Economics for Business; Business Communication; Introduction to Management; Business Law; Quantitative Methods
Year 2: Marketing Principles; Organisational Behaviour; Finance for Business; Business Ethics and Sustainability; Human Resource Management; Business Statistics
Year 3: specialisation strand (four units in Management, Marketing, International Business or Hospitality Management) plus Strategic Management and a capstone business project
Capstone: industry-linked business project or case competition in the final trimester

name: Bachelor of Fashion Business
description:
Bachelor of Fashion Business is Holmes's attempt to sit between a straight business degree and a design school program. It teaches merchandising, buying, retail management and fashion marketing rather than pattern-making or garment construction, so students who actually want to design clothes should look elsewhere (RMIT or Whitehouse Institute are the more obvious choices in that space). What this degree is for is the commercial side of the fashion industry: supply chain, brand management, retail analytics and marketing applied specifically to apparel and accessories categories.

It shares a business core with Holmes's other undergraduate business degrees in years one and two, then narrows into fashion-specific units (trend forecasting, fashion retail management, visual merchandising) in year three. Melbourne's retail and wholesale fashion sector gives students some access to local industry placements and guest lecturers, though the program is smaller and less established than Holmes's mainstream business and accounting degrees, and prospective students should treat it as a niche offering rather than a flagship one.
curriculum:
Year 1: Accounting for Business Decisions; Introduction to Fashion Industry; Business Communication; Economics for Business; Marketing Principles; Business Law
Year 2: Fashion Retail Management; Consumer Behaviour; Finance for Business; Brand Management; Supply Chain Fundamentals; Organisational Behaviour
Year 3: Fashion Buying and Merchandising; Trend Forecasting and Product Development; Visual Merchandising; Digital Marketing for Fashion; Strategic Management; capstone fashion business project

name: Bachelor of Information Systems
description:
This is a three-year degree for students who want an IT qualification with a business faculty attached rather than an engineering one: the difference matters, because the emphasis throughout is on systems that support organisations (databases, ERP-adjacent platforms, business analytics) rather than low-level programming or hardware. Holmes teaches it out of its Melbourne CBD and Sydney campuses to a mostly international cohort, many of whom are using the degree as a stepping stone toward the 189/190 skilled migration occupation lists that include ICT business analyst and systems analyst roles.

The 24-unit structure moves from foundational programming and database units in year one through systems analysis and network fundamentals in year two, before a final year that includes an IT project unit where students build and document a working system end to end. It suits someone who wants employable IT skills without committing to a heavier computer science or software engineering load, though students aiming specifically at software development roles at larger tech employers may find a more technically dense degree from a research university better positioned for that path.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Programming; Database Systems; Business Information Systems; Foundations of Business Communication; Accounting for Business Decisions; Quantitative Methods
Year 2: Systems Analysis and Design; Network Fundamentals; Web Application Development; Operating Systems; Business Law; Project Management Principles
Year 3: IT Project Management; Enterprise Systems; Cybersecurity Fundamentals; Data Analytics for Business; two electives
Capstone: IT systems project — students design, build and document a working information system for a simulated or partner organisation

name: Bachelor of Professional Accounting
description:
This is the undergraduate counterpart to Holmes's Master of Professional Accounting: a three-year, CPA Australia and CA ANZ accredited degree built around the mandated accounting core (financial accounting, management accounting, auditing, tax, corporate law) plus general business units in the earlier years. It's the more common entry point for school leavers or first-degree students who know from the outset that they want to sit for CPA or CA membership after graduating, rather than coming to accounting via a conversion master's later.

The degree's reputation rests less on Holmes's institutional prestige and more on the fact that accreditation requirements are set externally by the professional bodies, so the technical content lines up closely with what's taught at any accredited Australian accounting degree. Where Holmes differentiates is smaller cohort sizes in tutorials and, for many international students, direct progression pathways from Holmes's own diploma and foundation programs into this degree with credit.
curriculum:
Year 1: Accounting Systems and Processes; Economics for Business; Business Law; Quantitative Methods; Business Communication; Introduction to Management
Year 2: Financial Accounting; Management Accounting; Corporations Law; Financial Management; Business Information Systems; Organisational Behaviour
Year 3: Auditing and Assurance Services; Taxation Law; Advanced Financial Accounting; Ethics and Governance in Accounting; Strategic Management Accounting; capstone accounting project

name: Graduate Diploma of Business
description:
The Graduate Diploma of Business is Holmes's shorter, standalone postgraduate business qualification: eight units over roughly eight months full-time, sitting below the MBA in the institute's course ladder and often used either as a terminal qualification for someone wanting a fast credential upgrade, or as a stepping stone that later articulates into the MBA with advanced standing.

The unit mix covers the standard generalist ground (accounting, marketing, management, economics) without the specialisation and elective units that round out the full MBA, so it's a leaner degree by design. Students who complete it and want to continue can usually move into Holmes's MBA with credit for overlapping units, which is the more common path than treating the Graduate Diploma as a final destination.
curriculum:
Trimester 1: Accounting for Business Decisions; Economics for Business; Marketing Management; Management and Organisations in a Global Environment
Trimester 2: Finance for Business; Statistics and Research Methods for Business Decisions; Human Resource Management; Business Law and Ethics
Assessment: case-based assignments and a group consulting-style report in place of a thesis or major capstone

name: Master of Business Administration
description:
Holmes Institute's MBA runs across its Melbourne and Sydney campuses to a full-time cohort that's overwhelmingly international, and the teaching reflects that: small seminar-style classes rather than lecture halls, with a lot of case discussion drawn from Asia-Pacific trade and services examples rather than the US case studies that dominate most MBA texts. The core is twelve units, everything from Accounting for Business Decisions through to Competitive Strategy, completed in about eighteen months, after which students pick one specialisation and one elective to round out the degree.

Because Holmes is a smaller private provider rather than a sandstone university, the MBA doesn't carry the brand weight of a Group of Eight degree, and it's honest to say most graduates use it as a credential to move into management roles in mid-sized firms or to support a permanent migration pathway, not to break into top-tier consulting or investment banking. Where it does its job well is for someone who already has a business degree or several years of work experience and wants the generalist management toolkit (finance, strategy, people management, research methods) without relocating overseas or taking two years out of the workforce.
curriculum:
Trimester 1: Accounting for Business Decisions; Economics for Business; Management and Organisations in a Global Environment; Marketing Management
Trimester 2: Finance for Business; Statistics and Research Methods for Business Decisions; Leveraging Information Technology for Business Advantage; Human Resource Management
Trimester 3: Competitive Strategy; Corporate Governance and Ethics; International Business; Project Management
Final trimester: one specialisation unit (Marketing, International Business, Management or Hospitality Management) plus one elective
Capstone: applied strategy project addressing a real organisational problem, presented to faculty and industry panel
admission_requirements: An Australian bachelor's degree (or equivalent); or an Australian Graduate Diploma; or an Australian Graduate Certificate (or equivalent) plus a minimum of two years' demonstrable relevant industry experience; or an Advanced Diploma/Associate Degree (or equivalent) plus a minimum of five years' demonstrable relevant industry experience.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 6.0 with no band below 5.5 (or equivalent - e.g. completed Year 12 in English at an Australian high school, or a prior Australian qualification passed at ≥50%).

name: Master of Business Administration (Professional)
description:
The Professional variant of Holmes's MBA swaps the standard version's single specialisation-plus-elective tail for a much broader elective bank: eight core units and eight electives, which can be taken all from one specialisation to produce a focused MBA (Professional) in, say, marketing or international business, or spread across areas for a generalist qualification. It's aimed at students who want more say over the back half of their degree than the standard MBA structure allows.

In practice the two MBA products at Holmes overlap heavily in their core content (accounting, finance, economics, management, strategy), and the choice between them usually comes down to how much a student already knows they want to specialise versus keep options open. Neither carries the recruiting pull of an MBA from a AACSB-accredited research university, so it suits people building a management career step by step rather than those chasing a brand-name credential for a lateral move into strategy consulting.
curriculum:
Core (8 units): Accounting for Business Decisions; Finance for Business; Economics for Business; Marketing Management; Management and Organisations in a Global Environment; Statistics and Research Methods for Business Decisions; Competitive Strategy; Corporate Governance and Ethics
Electives (8 units): chosen from Marketing, International Business, Management or Hospitality Management strands, or mixed across strands for a generalist profile
Capstone: applied business project drawing on the student's chosen elective focus

name: Master of Professional Accounting
description:
The Master of Professional Accounting at Holmes is built to satisfy the CPA Australia and CA ANZ accreditation requirements for entry into those professional bodies, which is really the whole point of the degree for most people enrolled in it: it's a conversion course for graduates whose undergraduate degree wasn't in accounting and who need the full suite of core accounting units to sit the CPA Program or CA exams. It runs over roughly two years full-time across twelve to sixteen units depending on how much credit a student's prior degree earns them.

Because it's an accreditation-driven degree, the unit list is fairly fixed by the professional bodies rather than by Holmes itself: financial accounting, management accounting, auditing, taxation law, corporate law and finance all have to appear. What Holmes adds on top is smaller class sizes and, for many students, English-language academic support built into the first trimester, which matters given a large share of the cohort has come from non-English-medium undergraduate study.
curriculum:
Trimester 1: Accounting Systems and Processes; Financial Accounting; Economics for Business; Quantitative Methods for Business
Trimester 2: Management Accounting; Corporations Law; Taxation Law; Financial Management
Trimester 3: Auditing and Assurance Services; Advanced Financial Accounting; Business Law; Research Methods in Accounting
Final trimester: Ethics and Governance in Accounting; Strategic Management Accounting; two accounting electives aligned to CPA Program entry requirements
